exposure: Mode of delivery (Cesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
Type of Cesarean section (acute vs. elective)
Women with IBD who underwent Cesarean section
Women with IBD who underwent vaginal delivery
outcome: 30-day maternal postpartum abdominal and perineal surgical complications
cohort: Women with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) who gave birth to liveborn singletons in Denmark between 1997 and 2015
finding: Women with IBD who underwent Cesarean section had a significantly higher risk of 30-day postpartum surgical complications, particularly small bowel and colon surgery, compared to those who had a vaginal delivery, regardless of the type of Cesarean section or use of immunosuppressants.
mod_finding: Women with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) who underwent caesarean section had a higher risk of surgical complications compared to those who had a vaginal delivery.
